teaching.hint: How could you compare nodes at the same depth before choosing the value visible from the right?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Visibility is decided separately at each depth. The tree's left-to-right order at that depth identifies the visible node even when it lies in a left subtree.
solution_outline.approach: Traverse the tree breadth-first, processing one complete depth at a time. Visit nodes from left to right, append the value of the last node at that depth, and enqueue each node's left child before its right child for the next depth.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Before each depth is processed, the queue contains exactly the existing nodes at that depth in left-to-right order. Processing the whole group and enqueuing left children before right children establishes the same property for the next depth.
solution_outline.correctness: At each depth, the last queued node has no node farther right at that depth, so its value is exactly the one visible from the right. The queue invariant makes this true at every depth, and processing depths in order returns the values from top to bottom.
solution_outline.complexity: Every node is visited once, giving O(n) time and O(w) auxiliary queue space for maximum width w.
solution_outline.pitfall: Returning only nodes that have no right child mistakes a structural property for rightmost position; a left child can be visible.

accepted_alternatives: Depth-first traversal that visits right children before left children and records the first node reached at each depth.
common_wrong_turns: Ignoring visible left children when no right child exists
Appending every last child encountered without grouping by depth
Returning node values in bottom-up order
source_fidelity_notes: One source example was restated as a text tree to clarify what the right-side view includes; top-down order, empty-tree behavior, and node and value bounds were retained.
